Before Vivek Ramaswamy's now-infamous attack ad on his Democratic opponent
leaked last week, multiple Republicans on and close to his campaign warned the
Trump-endorsed Ohio GOP gubernatorial nominee that running this ad was a
terrible idea - explaining it would very likely backfire on him, make Democrat
Amy Acton seem more sympathetic to crucial median voters, and make him look
cruel and desperate, people familiar with the matter tell **Zeteo**.

Ramaswamy, of course, did it anyway.

"It's siding with the rapist protector mom," a Donald Trump adviser says about
the ad. "This was never a good idea," adds the adviser, who says they knew
about the ad before it was first published online by the "Rooster" Ohio
blogger.

The disturbing ad stars Acton's long-estranged mother Donna Arthur, who calls
the Democratic candidate a liar who deceived people about her past and
childhood; according to contemporaneous
[accounts](https://books.google.com/books?id=XSxJAAAAIBAJ&pg=PA2&dq=%22Cledith+Arthur%22&article_id=2363,3715254&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjKzZuj5ciXAxURMlkFHbrBM7kQ6AF6BAgKEAM#v=onepage&q&f=false)
and [court
documents](https://x.com/JustinBarasky/status/2112607893354693083/), the
mother's husband raped Acton when she was a child, and the mom defended him,
fled the state with him before a trial could happen, and stayed with him until
he died decades later.

This information was publicly available before the ad was made, before the
Ramaswamy campaign announced it would put millions of dollars into promoting
the ad, and before President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance publicly
embraced Team Vivek's new attack ad.

**Zeteo** can now reveal more on how the ad came together, and who else was
involved. Somehow, the depraved, sleazy story of how this happened - a new low
in a race that the _New York Times_ has declared likely the
"[ugliest](https://zeteo.com/p/the-ugliest-midterms-race-just-got)" in the
nation - is even worse than you already think it is. This includes details
about how visibly unwell Acton's elderly birth mother seemed when Team Vivek
tracked her down, and how "far gone" the alleged character witness acted when
the cameras were off, in the words of one top Ohio Republican.

We can also report that the firm that created the ad is the Strategy Group -
an Ohio-based firm that's come under fire for [handling
part](https://www.propublica.org/article/kristi-noem-dhs-ad-campaign-strategy-
group) of a sketchy $220 million Department of Homeland Security ad deal.
